trends.name: Iran Crisis & Oil Price Shock
trends.summary: Trump's Tuesday Iran deadline and threat to 'blow up everything' is triggering oil price spikes above $115/barrel WTI. Real-time X posts show Iran rejecting ceasefire terms and threatening retaliatory strikes on U.S. infrastructure. Oil volatility is now the primary market mover, with models showing CPI could hit 3.7% if elevated prices sustain 7+ weeks.

trends.name: AI Data Center Boom Strains Insurance
trends.summary: Massive private capital inflow into AI data centers is creating unprecedented insurance stress-testing and liability concerns. Maine's move to ban new data centers (with 10 other states considering similar restrictions) signals emerging regulatory headwinds for the AI infrastructure boom that was expected to anchor Q2-Q3 growth.

trends.name: S&P 500 Geopolitical Risk Exposure
trends.summary: Analysis of S&P 500 10-Ks reveals massive undisclosed geopolitical risk exposure: Morgan Stanley has 221 mentions of geopolitical risk, Citigroup 269. This indicates broad corporate vulnerability to Iran escalation, tariff wars, and supply chain disruptions—largely underpriced into current valuations.

trends.name: Crude Oil Prompt Spread Widening
trends.summary: Brent crude's prompt spread has widened to over $10/barrel, signaling severe near-term supply concerns and refinery stress. Combined with WTI +3% moves on Iran headlines, this is creating acute energy inflation risks for Q2 earnings, particularly impacting Delta and other consumer-facing sectors.

trends.name: IPO Market Stalled Despite Mega-Deals
trends.summary: Despite anticipated mega-IPOs from SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI, the broader IPO market remains structurally weak and unable to drive market breadth. HMH Holding noted as a rare public offering, indicating dried-up capital markets access for mid-cap companies amid geopolitical uncertainty.

trends.name: Fed Policy Uncertainty & Economic Data Week
trends.summary: FOMC Minutes (Wed), PCE Price Index (Thu), CPI March (Fri), and ISM Services PMI (Tue) converge this week amid elevated inflation from oil prices. Any CPI print above 3.2% would contradict Fed's disinflation narrative and trigger rate-hike repricing, particularly problematic with Iran war uncertainty.

trends.name: Baidu Valuation Play on AI Robotics
trends.summary: Baidu pivoting to AI infrastructure, robotaxis, and embodied robotics at a discount valuation. Represents potential alpha play for investors seeking China AI exposure with cheaper entry than Nvidia/TSM, but carries China geopolitical risk given Trump administration tensions.

trends.name: Trump Administration Dementia Concerns
trends.summary: Real-time X posts from financial journalists describe Trump exhibiting signs of cognitive decline (word-finding difficulties, confusion, illogical thought patterns). This raises critical uncertainty around policy coherence and Iran negotiation credibility, creating elevated tail-risk premium in markets.

trends.name: Dividend Portfolio Disruptions & SCHD
trends.summary: SCHD ETF experiencing significant internal changes impacting dividend investors and retirees. Shift in underlying holdings signals dividend yield sustainability questions and potential portfolio adjustments needed among income-focused investors, particularly vulnerable fixed-income segments.

trends.name: Corporate AI Value Capture Questions
trends.summary: IBM analysis reveals strong execution on AI but persistent questions around actual profit capture and ROI. Broader theme questioning whether AI infrastructure boom translates to earnings growth or remains speculative capital allocation by mega-cap tech firms.

trends.name: Asia Stock Recovery on Iran Deal Hopes
trends.summary: Japan and South Korea stocks rising as investors weigh Trump's extended Iran deadline and ceasefire discussion signals. Regional exposure to Middle East escalation and energy prices making Asia a hedge against U.S. energy-driven stagflation.

trends.name: Retail Gas Price Shock & Consumer Sentiment
trends.summary: Gas prices spiking above $4 is creating measurable deterioration in consumer sentiment, with psychological impact worse than 2022-2023 episodes. This threatens Q2 consumer spending and earnings guidance amid already-strained household finances and April seasonality headwinds.
